source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Give the sow plenty of water on the day she farrows but do not feed her that day; give 30–50% of her normal ration on day two, then gradually increase to as much as she'll eat over the following 5 days, feeding ad-lib from day 5 onward. Make sure every piglet drinks from the sow within the first 2 hours of life — the first milk (colostrum) contains special proteins that protect the piglet from disease. After a piglet has been suckled, paint its umbilical cord with iodine solution and place it in the creep box for warmth. Castrate male piglets between 3 and 7 days old. Inject all piglets with iron on the same day (ask a veterinary technician before combining iron with penicillin, since Streptococcus bacteria can otherwise cause arthritis or brain infection). Treat sow and piglets for parasites 7 days before weaning.
caveat: Medication names and dosages are reproduced from the source manual for reference only. Product availability, correct dosing, and withdrawal periods vary by country and should be confirmed with a local veterinarian or extension officer before use.
